C1.rationale: Level 2 anchor: 'At least one core unit assesses collaborative practice — group projects with individual accountability' is satisfied by the compulsory Data Analysis subject's syndicate assignment, graded 'equivalent to individual' work. Level 3 additionally requires an assessment where 'coordinating work across people AND tools/AI systems' is itself assessed; no such assessed division of labour between people and AI/tools appears anywhere in the extract, so the program does not clear level 3.
evidenceLines: Students are required to achieve a grade of 70% minimum in Data Analysis to progress to Category 2 and Category 3 subjects and students cannot continue in the Master of Analytics Management course without meeting all the requirements below.

C2.rationale: Level 0 anchor: 'No assessment requires students to appraise the quality of work — their own, peers', or a tool's.' Every assessment breakdown captured in the extract (contribution items, quizzes, syndicate assignments, exams) contains no peer-review, criterion-referenced critique, portfolio-with-standards, or reliance-decision component. 'instructor evaluation of contribution to class learning' is staff appraising the student, not the student appraising work, so it does not satisfy the construct.
evidenceLines: Contribution to class learning: Attendance at lectures and workshops, instructor evaluation of contribution to class learning

C3.rationale: Ambiguous between level 1 ('AI or digital tools appear only as electives or as tool operation/training') and level 2 ('Core units address AI capabilities AND limitations/ethics ... discussed and assessed'). MGMT90244 Leading Data and AI Transformation is listed in Category 2 without a 'choose N of M' qualifier — unlike Category 1's 'any three of the following five' and Category 3's 'any two of the following three' — so it reads as required, and its outcomes state an 'ethical framework for how to use business analytics', which is not tool-operation content. But the subject's assessment table only names generic categories (in-class contribution, quizzes, final exam) with no line tying an assessment task to the ethics/governance content, so per R2 the assessed status of that content cannot be confirmed. Resolved to the lower level (1); ambiguity recorded.

C4.rationale: Level 2 anchor: 'At least one core assessment requires application to novel or unfamiliar problems'. Applied Analytics Lab, the required Category 4 capstone, requires students to 'articulate the business problem to be solved' using 'real data from an industry setting', assessed via a hurdle project proposal and a final report/presentation. Level 3 requires a demonstrably self-scoped capstone, or assessed identification of one's own knowledge gaps with a plan to close them; the extract states only that the project uses real industry data, not that students select or scope the project themselves, so self-scoping cannot be confirmed. Resolved to the lower level (2); ambiguity recorded.
evidenceLines: This subject involves completion of a 10-week project using real data from an industry setting.

C5.rationale: Level 2 anchor: 'Students design and conduct an inquiry with methodology selection and data collection, assessed'. Applied Analytics Lab requires students to 'articulate the business problem to be solved and the data & tools required' and to 'produce original work ... which demonstrates analytical, research and problem-solving skills', using real industry data, assessed through a hurdle project proposal and a report-plus-30-minute-presentation. Level 3 requires the methodology to be 'defended under scrutiny (viva, defence, or staged supervised review)'; the extract documents only a presentation of the report, not an interrogation of method, so level 3 cannot be confirmed. Resolved to the lower level (2); ambiguity recorded.

W1.rationale: Ambiguous between level 1 ('core assessment adds presentation to peers/staff, but no professional genre and no audience beyond the teaching team') and level 2 (a 'recognised professional genre or an audience beyond the teaching team ... judged against criteria drawn from professional practice'). Applied Analytics Lab's capstone requires students to 'present their work professionally in a way that makes the connections between the results of their analysis and business issues for an organisation', suggestive of a consultancy-style genre, and Marketing includes a syndicate presentation. But the extract never names either presentation's audience, so it cannot be confirmed as extending beyond the teaching team or as judged against professional-practice criteria. Resolved to the lower level (1); ambiguity recorded.

W2.rationale: Level 2 anchor: 'At least one core assessment reproduces a professional task end to end: a real or realistic problem, producing the artefact a practitioner would produce, judged against criteria drawn from practice.' Applied Analytics Lab is 'completion of a 10-week project using real data from an industry setting', producing a report and presentation that 'makes the connections between the results of their analysis and business issues for an organisation' — the artefact an analyst would produce, from a real problem. Level 3 requires such tasks to be the program's 'assessment spine ... at least one per stage'; earlier categories document syndicate case assignments and reports built on business scenarios rather than full real-data professional-task reproduction, so the spine condition is not met.
evidenceLines: This subject involves completion of a 10-week project using real data from an industry setting.

W3.rationale: Level 0 anchor: 'No work-integrated learning, placement, practicum or community-based project appears anywhere in the course structure.' No placement, practicum, internship or community-based project is named anywhere in the extract. The closest candidate is Applied Analytics Lab's 'real data from an industry setting', but the text documents a data-analysis project rather than a workplace placement, and never states practitioner supervision, a host organisation, or accountability to that host, which level 2 ('real workplace or professional-community setting with practitioner supervision and assessment') requires. Because the evidence is genuinely ambiguous as to whether this constitutes work-situated learning at all, it is resolved to the lower level (0); ambiguity recorded.
evidenceLines: This subject involves completion of a 10-week project using real data from an industry setting.
